newsitem.title: USA: USDA probing if tainted strawberries from Mexico.
newsitem.headline: USDA probing if tainted strawberries from Mexico.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Department is investigating whether tainted strawberries that sickened over 100 school children in Michigan came from Mexico, department sources said Wednesday.
"It looks like the products were grown in Mexico, which means the company was in violation of the law," said the sources, who spoke on condition of anonymity.
Companies must certify in writing by law that the products they sell to the goverment school lunch program are grown in the United States.
USDA's Office of Inspector General has launched a probe into the matter, the sources said.
Last week, school officials in Michigan reported an outbreak of Hepatitis A. Federal health officials traced the source to frozen strawberries purchased by USDA for the school lunch program.
Seventeen states received the tainted berries. Michigan and five other states received the same lot of strawberries.
USDA was expected to issue a formal statement later Wednesday.
